root_cause_label: Environment obstacle triggers abandonment of scipy, agent falls back to naive grid search over under-parameterized two-part distribution that cannot satisfy dual KL constraints
one_sentence_failure_summary: After failing to install scipy into the active venv, the agent abandoned numerical optimization entirely and spent all remaining steps cycling through coarse grid searches over under-parameterized distributions that are mathematically incapable of simultaneously satisfying both KL=10 constraints.
t_err_evidence: Step 7: Agent rewrites the solution without scipy, replacing a proper optimizer with a naive grid search over a two-part distribution parameterized only by k (number of high-prob tokens) and a single ratio; this parameterization lacks sufficient degrees of freedom to satisfy both forward and backward KL=10 simultaneously.
t_commit_evidence: Step 7 locks in the wrong strategy (grid search on 2-part distribution); from this point the agent never reconsiders using scipy or a root-finding method, and every subsequent attempt is a variant of the same insufficient approach.
t_surface_evidence: Step 8 first execution shows 'Solution does not meet tolerance requirements': Forward KL=5.93, Backward KL=9.17, both far from target 10.0.
trigger_explanation: Scipy IS installed at /usr/local/lib/python3.13 but the active venv at /opt/openhands-venv/bin/python lacks it. The agent tried `pip install scipy` (system pip, not venv pip) and then `python -m pip install scipy` (venv has no pip). Rather than fixing the venv path issue (e.g., install scipy into venv directly or invoke /usr/local/bin/python), the agent abandoned scipy entirely and switched to an insufficient pure-numpy grid search approach.
forewarning_evidence: Steps 2, 4, 6 all show ModuleNotFoundError for scipy or 'No module named pip', signaling the environment path problem before the agent makes its decisive pivot at step 7.
